PDVSA Appoints New Chief Financial Officer Amid Push for Enhanced Transparency

Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA), Venezuela’s state-run oil and gas producer, announced Tuesday the appointment of Maria Fernanda Salazar as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective immediately. The move comes as the company seeks to strengthen financial oversight and improve transparency amid ongoing efforts to stabilize production and attract investment.

Salazar, a 20-year veteran of the energy sector, previously served as deputy finance director at Energia Andina and has held various financial leadership roles within the country’s oil and gas industry. She replaces Gustavo Jimenez, who is retiring after more than three decades with the company.

In a statement, PDVSA President Rafael Quiroz welcomed Salazar’s appointment, citing her “deep understanding of financial operations and commitment to international best practices.” Quiroz added, “Salazar’s experience will be crucial as we pursue greater efficiency in all aspects of our business, aiming to restore confidence among stakeholders and partners.”

Industry analysts see the leadership change as a positive step for PDVSA, which has faced challenges in recent years due to fluctuating global oil prices and domestic economic pressures. “Bringing in a CFO with Salazar’s credentials signals the company’s intent to enhance financial discipline,” said Luis Herrera, senior analyst at the Caracas Energy Institute. “It’s a move that could help improve reporting standards and facilitate negotiations with potential investors.”

The Venezuelan Oilworkers Federation also expressed support for the appointment. Federation spokesperson Ana Delgado stated, “We welcome professionals who can contribute to the stability and growth of our industry.”

PDVSA, which accounts for the majority of Venezuela’s export revenue, has not indicated any immediate changes to its financial outlook or operational strategy in connection with the appointment.
